sections.title: Render from state
sections.description: A component returns **JSX** from its current props and state. Event handlers update state; the renderer reconciles the resulting tree.

sections.title: Own the lifecycle
sections.description: Allocate browser work inside an effect and return its cleanup. This keeps **listeners, timers and subscriptions** tied to the component that needs them.
sections.note: Browser globals belong behind an effect or an explicit environment check when rendering on the server.

sections.title: Keep the renderer clear
sections.description: React and Preact share familiar component concepts, but their **renderers, hooks and types** are separate dependencies. Kamod components are authored for Preact.

sections.title: Check compatibility
sections.description: A compatibility alias translates selected React entry points. It does not turn every React integration into a supported Preact API or remove the need to test its behavior.

code.value:
// Compatibility is configured by the application.
"react": "preact/compat"
"react-dom": "preact/compat"
"react/jsx-runtime": "preact/jsx-runtime"
code.caption: Alias illustration

sections.note: Prefer native Preact packages for new Kamod compositions; retain deliberate aliases for existing integrations.

sections.title: Describe the contract
sections.description: Type aliases and interfaces make component inputs explicit. An optional property permits omission; a union limits the accepted values.

sections.title: Validate runtime input
sections.description: Type information is erased from emitted JavaScript. Data from a form, URL or service still needs **runtime validation** before it can be trusted.
sections.note: Use a schema library when a boundary needs structured errors or inferred output types.

sections.title: Make updates explicit
sections.description: Use functions and immutable collection updates to make the transition from **old state to new state** visible in application code.

rows.label: Browser behavior
rows.value: Events, DOM APIs and asynchronous work

sections.title: Finish asynchronous work
sections.description: A promise can outlive the view that started it. Cancel supported requests or ignore obsolete results when the owner is disposed or the input changes.
sections.note: Cancellation and rejection handling are separate responsibilities; display only errors relevant to the current request.

sections.title: Follow the source
sections.description: Repository files explain how a component is implemented; pull requests explain a proposed change and its validation. Prefer a **specific file or package** when citing code.

sections.title: Review the change
sections.description: A useful review connects the diff, its tests and the resulting behavior. Branch links follow new commits; a commit permalink preserves the exact version being discussed.
sections.note: A successful old check does not verify a newer head commit.

sections.title: Inspect before editing
sections.description: The working tree, index and current branch describe different states. Read the diff before staging so an unrelated local adjustment is not bundled into a feature.

code.value:
git status --short
git diff --stat
git diff -- path/to/file

sections.title: Stage a focused change
sections.description: Explicit paths make a commit reviewable and preserve local-only context. The staged diff is the content the next commit records.

code.value:
git add path/to/changed-file
git diff --cached
git commit

sections.note: Generated build output and local context should not be swept into a formatting commit.

sections.title: Retain the existing check
sections.description: The root configuration keeps Biome alongside Oxlint and Oxfmt. Its configured checks remain part of repository validation.

code.value: corepack pnpm biome:ci

sections.title: Avoid conflicting rewrites
sections.description: Run the project's check command after formatting. If two tools disagree, inspect the configured rule and make the smallest targeted correction rather than reformatting the repository.
sections.note: Do not remove an existing validation layer simply because another tool covers part of the same area.

sections.title: Build package entry points
sections.description: Package build configuration determines which public modules are emitted. Keep entry points aligned with `package.json` exports when exposing a new component or block.

sections.title: Restore runtime output
sections.description: Type-only output cannot satisfy a consumer that imports built JavaScript. In this workspace, rebuild after declaration-only typechecking before tests that consume package distributions.

code.value:
corepack pnpm typecheck
corepack pnpm build

sections.note: Check both the declaration contract and the runtime entry that a package consumer actually imports.

sections.title: Understand the output graph
sections.description: A module bundler starts from entry points and follows imports to produce distributable files. Entry selection, externals and output format determine what consumers receive.

rows.label: Entry
rows.value: A public application or library module

rows.label: External
rows.value: A dependency left for the consumer

sections.title: Inspect the emitted bundle
sections.description: Tree shaking depends on analyzable modules and side-effect information. Verify the generated assets rather than inferring bundle size from a short import statement.

code.value: import { Button } from "@kamod-ch/ui/button";
code.caption: Focused public entry point

sections.note: Consult the current build configuration before assuming a particular bundler backend or plugin is active.

sections.title: Check the configured backend
sections.description: Rolldown is a JavaScript bundler with a Rust implementation. Its public configuration and plugin compatibility should be checked against the installed build-tool version.

sections.title: Treat migration as behavior
sections.description: A bundler change can affect chunk boundaries, dependency interoperation and emitted assets. Recheck dynamic imports and deployed route prefixes even when source files are unchanged.
sections.note: Rollup-compatible API goals do not remove the need to validate the plugins used by this project.

sections.title: Separate transforms and checks
sections.description: esbuild transforms and bundles source. Transpiling TypeScript removes type syntax; it does not replace the repository's TypeScript checking stage.

rows.label: Bundle
rows.value: Resolve and combine the module graph

rows.label: Typecheck
rows.value: Run the project's compiler checks separately

sections.title: Respect runtime dependencies
sections.description: Library builds often keep framework peers external so consumers share one renderer. Verify package metadata and emitted imports when changing entry points.

rows.label: Validation
rows.value: Import the built output, not only the source

sections.note: A fast successful build is useful evidence about output, not proof of runtime behavior.

sections.title: Read the plugin pipeline
sections.description: PostCSS parses CSS and lets configured plugins transform it. Its presence alone does not identify which transformations an application applies.

rows.label: Parser
rows.value: CSS source into a syntax tree

rows.label: Output
rows.value: CSS passed to the next build stage

sections.title: Avoid duplicate styling owners
sections.description: This docs app connects Tailwind through its Vite plugin. Add another CSS pipeline only for a verified requirement and inspect the resulting import order.
sections.note: A third-party PostCSS recipe may describe a different Tailwind version or integration.

sections.title: Transform for browser targets
sections.description: Autoprefixer is a PostCSS plugin that adds vendor prefixes according to configured browser support data. It is distinct from a utility CSS generator.

sections.title: Verify before adding it
sections.description: Check the current Tailwind integration and build pipeline before copying an older setup command. Duplicate transforms add complexity without establishing broader browser support.
sections.note: Prefix generation does not implement every missing browser feature.

sections.title: Recognize a different rule engine
sections.description: ESLint checks code through its configured parser, rules and plugins. An ESLint example may be useful in a consumer project while this repository uses Oxlint as its primary linter.

source.label: ESLint: Recognize a different rule engine

sections.title: Transfer the requirement
sections.description: When a guide mentions an ESLint rule, identify the actual requirement—hook ordering, unused values or accessibility—then verify the corresponding project checks.

rows.label: Regression
rows.value: A focused test for observable behavior

sections.note: Do not add a second lint stack solely to reproduce an external guide's command.

sections.title: Keep formatter ownership clear
sections.description: Prettier formats source in projects that select it. This checkout uses Oxfmt, so retain the existing formatter configuration when adapting examples.

code.value: corepack pnpm format:check
code.caption: Repository formatting check

sections.title: Separate formatting and semantics
sections.description: Formatting should preserve behavior and make a diff easier to read. Review substantive changes separately from generated whitespace or unrelated formatting churn.
sections.note: Use explicit changed-file paths when applying formatting locally.

sections.title: Choose the interactive island
sections.description: Astro can combine static page content with selectively interactive components. A component's hydration boundary determines when browser behavior becomes available.

rows.label: Renderer
rows.value: The integration selected by the application

sections.title: Keep one owner per island
sections.description: A Kamod composition needs a Preact-compatible boundary and its global theme styles. State, overlay ownership and focus handling should remain inside the deliberate integration.

source.label: Astro: Keep one owner per island

rows.label: Theme
rows.value: Import the chosen global stylesheet once

rows.label: Overlays
rows.value: Test portals and focus across the island boundary

sections.note: This checkout does not require Astro to run or document its Preact components.

sections.title: Read the selected version
sections.description: Remix is a web framework with its own application and routing contracts. Use the documentation for the version in the consumer rather than assuming an external example matches this project.

sections.title: Keep blocks framework-independent
sections.description: Pass navigation and application state into reusable compositions. A block should not require a framework-specific route module or authentication implementation to render its layout.
sections.note: Verify the renderer integration before adopting a framework's component example.

sections.title: Recognize compiled components
sections.description: Svelte compiles its component format into application code. A Svelte component is not interchangeable with a Preact component merely because both render HTML.

rows.label: Shared layer
rows.value: HTML semantics and CSS design roles

sections.title: Port the visual contract
sections.description: When a design reference comes from Svelte, reuse its layout ideas while keeping Kamod's existing state, focus and overlay primitives. Translate the interaction rather than copying incompatible component syntax.

rows.label: Portable
rows.value: Content hierarchy, spacing and semantic colors

sections.note: A separate renderer boundary is an application integration choice, not a default block dependency.

sections.title: Keep component models distinct
sections.description: Vue provides its own component and reactivity APIs. Kamod implementations use Preact props, hooks and JSX types, so examples need a deliberate translation at that boundary.

sections.title: Translate state ownership
sections.description: A port should preserve which value controls the interaction and how changes reach the caller. Reuse a Kamod controlled/uncontrolled API rather than adding a parallel state model.

rows.label: Change callback
rows.value: How the caller learns about an update

rows.label: Lifecycle
rows.value: Cleanup owned by the Preact view

sections.note: Template syntax and framework-specific directives do not become valid TSX by copying them.

sections.title: Render mathematical notation
sections.description: KaTeX converts supported mathematical source into web markup. Inline formulas and display formulas serve different layout roles.

rows.label: Presentation
rows.value: The required KaTeX stylesheet and output markup

sections.title: Handle invalid expressions
sections.description: Unsupported commands or invalid notation need a readable failure state. Choose deliberate error handling instead of allowing one formula to fail an entire document render.

rows.label: Default failure
rows.value: A parse error can be thrown

rows.label: Content policy
rows.value: Control trusted commands and external links

sections.note: Typesetting support and safe handling of untrusted author input are separate decisions.

sections.title: Parse a human date
sections.description: The date-picker example uses `parseDate` with a reference date and a forward-date preference. Parsing is separate from how the resulting date is displayed or saved.

code.value:
import { parseDate } from "chrono-node";
const parsed = parseDate(value, referenceDate, { forwardDate: true });

sections.title: Keep ambiguity visible
sections.description: Relative phrases depend on the reference date and parsing context. Show the resolved date before committing a consequential change and handle an unrecognized phrase explicitly.

rows.label: Output
rows.value: A resolved date or no result

sections.note: A parsed Date does not by itself establish the user's intended time zone or business deadline.

sections.title: Distinguish example and dependency
sections.description: React DayPicker is a calendar library with its own renderer integration. Kamod's calendar documentation is not evidence that the core component depends on that package.

sections.title: Preserve date interaction
sections.description: When adapting a calendar example, verify focus movement, disabled dates, selection mode and locale behavior. Matching its visual grid does not reproduce those contracts.

rows.label: Selection
rows.value: Single date, range or multiple values

rows.label: Keyboard
rows.value: A reachable and predictable focused date

rows.label: Locale
rows.value: Week start, labels and formatted output

sections.note: Choose a native Preact implementation or a deliberately tested compatibility boundary.

sections.title: Assemble conditional classes
sections.description: clsx collects strings and conditional values into a class string. It decides which classes are present; it does not resolve competing Tailwind utilities.

code.value: clsx("inline-flex", active && "font-semibold", { "opacity-50": disabled });

sections.title: Use the shared composition
sections.description: Kamod's `cn` utility feeds conditional class assembly into Tailwind conflict resolution. Consumers can override a default without duplicating this two-stage behavior.

code.caption: The two-stage cn pipeline

sections.note: A class string still needs complete utility names discoverable by the CSS build.

sections.title: Resolve utility conflicts
sections.description: Tailwind Merge removes recognized conflicting utility classes according to its class-group rules. It operates on class names rather than computed browser styles.

code.value:
twMerge("px-2 py-1", "px-4");
// Keeps the later horizontal padding and the vertical padding.

sections.title: Keep configuration compatible
sections.description: Use the version and configuration matched to the project's Tailwind vocabulary. Custom utilities and variants may need explicit support rather than being recognized automatically.

rows.label: Input
rows.value: A class string assembled by clsx

sections.note: It does not inspect stylesheets, evaluate selectors or guarantee a particular computed visual result.

sections.title: Separate engine and layout
sections.description: Embla supplies the scrolling engine while Kamod provides the component composition. The viewport, track and slides each retain their structural role.

sections.title: Dispose engine subscriptions
sections.description: Selection listeners and engine state belong to the mounted carousel. Detach subscribed callbacks when replacing the engine or unmounting the owning component.

rows.label: Update
rows.value: Read the selected slide and control availability

rows.label: Cleanup
rows.value: Remove listeners and destroy the owned instance

sections.note: Slide count and width affect available movement; test controls at both ends rather than assuming they always scroll.

sections.title: Make motion optional
sections.description: The autoplay plugin advances slides automatically. A pause control lets someone stop the movement without losing access to manual navigation.

sections.title: Stop when appropriate
sections.description: Coordinate autoplay with user interaction, hidden content and reduced-motion preferences. The timer should not continue consuming resources after its carousel is disposed.

rows.label: Interaction
rows.value: A deliberate pause or stop policy

rows.label: Reduced motion
rows.value: Prefer a quiet or stopped initial state

sections.note: Autoplay must remain an enhancement; every slide should still be reachable without waiting.

sections.title: Define a variant contract
sections.description: A variant recipe groups base classes and named choices. Components can expose semantic options instead of scattering repeated utility strings through every caller.

source.label: Tailwind Variants: Define a variant contract

rows.label: Variants
rows.value: Named dimensions such as size or intent

sections.title: Keep API and style aligned
sections.description: Document which variant names are public and what they change. Forward a consumer class deliberately and keep disabled, focus and responsive behavior in the same recipe.

code.value: <Button variant="outline" size="sm">Continue</Button>
code.caption: A semantic component-facing contract

sections.note: Read the component's actual prop type; a style recipe does not make arbitrary variant names valid.

sections.title: Choose the individual library
sections.description: TanStack is a family of libraries, not one installable behavior. Table, Query, Router and other products solve different problems and have separate integration contracts.

sections.title: Keep state ownership explicit
sections.description: Adopting a headless library should replace a defined responsibility rather than duplicate it. Decide which layer owns data fetching, pagination or table state before connecting the UI.

rows.label: Headless library
rows.value: Its selected state or computation model

sections.note: A React example is not the default integration contract for a Preact application.

sections.title: Separate table logic and markup
sections.description: Headless table logic computes a row model while the application renders accessible table elements. Sorting and pagination state must be connected to the chosen data owner.

sections.title: Read this example's implementation
sections.description: Kamod's current data-table example uses local Preact state. Its appearance is not a claim that TanStack Table is installed or required for the primitive.

rows.label: Current demo
rows.value: Local sorting, filtering and pagination state

sections.note: Use the adapter and API documented for the version installed by the consuming application.

sections.title: Parse the authoring format
sections.description: Marked turns Markdown source into tokens or HTML. Parsing gives the document structure; the application chooses the rendering and trust policy.

sections.title: Keep HTML trust separate
sections.description: Do not insert arbitrary parsed HTML into the page without sanitizing or otherwise enforcing the application's content policy. Link destinations and raw HTML need their own checks.
sections.note: A Markdown parser is not an HTML sanitizer.

sections.title: Simulate the DOM
sections.description: jsdom provides a document environment for Node-based component tests. It supports DOM assertions without starting a full graphical browser.

code.value:
/** @vitest-environment jsdom */
import { render } from "@testing-library/preact";

sections.title: Use a browser for geometry
sections.description: Responsive sizes, clipping, scroll placement and visual contrast need browser evidence. Mocking a rectangle can test placement logic but cannot verify real rendered layout.

source.label: jsdom: Use a browser for geometry

rows.label: Cleanup
rows.value: Unmount and restore mocks between cases

sections.note: A jsdom test should not claim visual compatibility with Chrome or Safari.

sections.title: Keep generated identity stable
sections.description: The optional SmartAvatar recipe derives a repeatable generated fallback from a stable name or user identifier. Core Avatar remains the underlying primitive.

code.value: <SmartAvatar name="stable-user-id" />
code.caption: Optional documentation recipe

sections.title: Opt into motion deliberately
sections.description: The guide imports Blobatar motion styles only for animated fallbacks. Static avatars and ordinary remote photos do not need that animation layer.

code.value: @import "blobatar/motion.css";

sections.note: Verify missing, failed and slow image states; a fallback should not change a user's visual identity on every render.

sections.title: Build an archive from source
sections.description: Documentation download scripts encode each source file and construct a ZIP archive at build time. The browser receives the generated artifact rather than running the archive builder.

source.label: fflate: Build an archive from source

code.value:
import { strToU8, zipSync } from "fflate";
const archive = zipSync({ "example.ts": strToU8(source) });

sections.title: Make downloads reproducible
sections.description: The block exporters set stable archive timestamps and preserve exact destination paths. Tests unzip the result to verify the file inventory and source content.
sections.note: Synchronous compression belongs in the build script here, not the tooltip or an idle animation loop.

sections.title: Audit rendered markup
sections.description: axe-core runs automated accessibility rules over a document. The Playwright integration lets this repository audit pages in a real browser state.

code.value: corepack pnpm test:a11y

sections.title: Interpret the scope
sections.description: Check the rule result, affected nodes and tested state. A passing automated scan cannot verify every keyboard flow, understandable label or assistive-technology experience.

rows.label: Evidence
rows.value: The page and state actually audited

sections.note: Keep hidden, expanded and error states in the verification plan when they change the interaction.

sections.title: Render without a browser
sections.description: The renderer converts a Preact tree to HTML for server rendering and markup tests. It does not run a browser layout engine or client-side effects.

code.value:
import { renderToString } from "preact-render-to-string"; const html = renderToString(

Ready

);

sections.title: Keep server output deterministic
sections.description: Browser globals, per-user storage and random values can make server output unsafe or inconsistent with the client. Provide stable initial state and defer browser-only work to effects.
sections.note: A render-to-string assertion verifies markup, not effect cleanup or final visual layout.

sections.title: Use the shared animation layer
sections.description: The documentation stylesheet imports `tw-animate-css` alongside its other global styling. Component state classes can then select the intended animation treatment.

source.label: tw-animate-css: Use the shared animation layer

code.value: @import "tw-animate-css";
code.caption: From the documentation stylesheet

sections.title: Avoid competing animation owners
sections.description: The motion guide keeps CSS animation classes and motion presets off the same nodes. Choose one owner so transforms and timing do not fight each other.
sections.note: Decorative loops should stop when their content is no longer mounted or relevant.

sections.title: Run repository hooks
sections.description: Lefthook dispatches the configured Git hooks. This repository's hook configuration runs checks on staged paths before a commit is recorded.

rows.label: Input
rows.value: Files selected in the Git index

sections.title: Keep checks reproducible
sections.description: Hooks support the contributor workflow, while explicit check commands make validation visible and repeatable. Inspect a hook failure and correct its cause before retrying.

code.value:
git diff --cached --stat
corepack pnpm lint
corepack pnpm format:check

sections.note: A hook validates its configured scope; it does not imply every test suite has run.

sections.title: Audit the dependency surface
sections.description: Knip reports candidates such as unused files, exports and dependencies. The result depends on entry points and tooling configuration, especially generated or virtual routes.

code.value: corepack pnpm knip

sections.title: Verify before removing
sections.description: A statically unused symbol may still be an intentional public export or a build-generated entry. Check package exports and route plugins before deleting a reported candidate.

rows.label: Evidence
rows.value: A real consumer or emitted bundle

sections.note: Treat reports as review candidates rather than blanket deletion instructions.

sections.title: Check workspace versions
sections.description: Syncpack audits dependency declarations across packages. The repository exposes a read-only lint command alongside an explicit version-fix command.

code.value: corepack pnpm syncpack:check

sections.title: Preserve dependency intent
sections.description: A peer range describes consumer compatibility, while a development dependency selects local tooling. Align versions only when those different responsibilities permit it.
sections.note: Version alignment is not a reason to widen a peer contract that has not been tested.

sections.title: Inspect the published shape
sections.description: publint checks package metadata against the built package. It helps catch publication problems that a source-only typecheck does not exercise.

code.value: corepack pnpm qa:publint

sections.title: Build before checking
sections.description: Run the affected library build so the checker can inspect the actual files referenced by exports. Keep public names, output filenames and declaration paths aligned.
sections.note: Metadata checks complement, rather than replace, importing and testing the built API.

sections.title: Check consumer type resolution
sections.description: Are the Types Wrong inspects how a package's declarations resolve for different module environments. This workspace exposes it through the `attw` verification scripts.

source.label: Are the Types Wrong: Check consumer type resolution

code.value: corepack pnpm qa:attw

sections.title: Align runtime and declarations
sections.description: A valid declaration file is useful only if consumers resolve it alongside the matching runtime export. Review export conditions when ESM and CommonJS consumers behave differently.

source.label: Are the Types Wrong: Align runtime and declarations

sections.note: Build the package before interpreting resolution diagnostics about its emitted files.

sections.title: Read checks for the commit
sections.description: A workflow run belongs to a specific revision and trigger. Review the run associated with the current pull-request head before treating automation as merge evidence.

source.label: GitHub Actions: Read checks for the commit

sections.title: Keep validation attributable
sections.description: A useful check reports the exact command, package scope and failure. Local success can help reproduce a problem, but it should not be presented as a remote workflow result.
sections.note: A newly pushed commit requires its own checks even when its parent passed.

sections.title: Read structured configuration
sections.description: YAML uses indentation to describe mappings and sequences. This workspace uses it for its package inventory and Git-hook configuration, among other tool inputs.

code.value:
packages:
  - packages/*
code.caption: Workspace package pattern

sections.title: Keep syntax and schema separate
sections.description: Valid YAML can still contain an invalid workflow or tool setting. Check the consuming tool's schema and preserve indentation when changing nested values.

source.label: YAML: Keep syntax and schema separate

rows.label: Schema
rows.value: Keys and values accepted by the consuming tool

sections.note: Quote values when their intended string meaning would otherwise be ambiguous.

sections.title: Distinguish inspiration and runtime
sections.description: The docs mention Radix-style patterns, but Kamod supplies its own Preact interaction primitives. Similar API names do not establish a Radix dependency.

sections.title: Reuse established behavior
sections.description: Port a reference by composing the existing Kamod trigger, content and state APIs. Verify keyboard operation, focus restoration and dismissal rather than introducing another overlay implementation.

rows.label: Content
rows.value: The matching Kamod panel or overlay

sections.note: New native Preact blocks should not add React-only Radix dependencies.

sections.title: Identify the stylesheet format
sections.description: Sass is a stylesheet language compiled to CSS. SCSS uses CSS-like braces; recognizing an `.scss` file does not mean the current app has enabled a Sass compiler.

rows.label: Current theme setup
rows.value: CSS imports and semantic custom properties

sections.title: Choose runtime tokens deliberately
sections.description: Sass variables are resolved during compilation, while CSS custom properties remain available to the browser. Theme switching needs the runtime token contract used by Kamod components.

code.value:
:root { --primary: #a21caf; }
.action { background: var(--primary); }
code.caption: Runtime CSS token illustration

sections.note: Adding a preprocessor is unnecessary when the existing CSS and Tailwind pipeline already expresses the requirement.
